intro: The applications that are live today, each with a working link and a plain description of what it does. This list is rebuilt automatically whenever a new application is added. Private business files and internal tools are left out on purpose.

apps.desc: The evidence foundation. World religions and Christian denominations scored against Scripture, the contested New Testament passages studied in the original Hebrew and Greek, the Millennial test, and how each of Amit's conclusions was reached.

apps.desc: Scripture study and original worship songs side by side. Full story-format studies for the feasts (Passover, Unleavened Bread, Firstfruits, Shavuot, Trumpets, Yom Kippur, Tabernacles) and a Difficult Passages page that begins with Colossians 2. Every study has a Speak to Me button.

apps.desc: The player for Amit's worship songs, with lyrics and video: Blow the Shofar for the Feast of Trumpets and When I See the Blood for Passover.

apps.name: Amit's Living Testimony

apps.name: AmitChat
apps.desc: A private, login-based chat inside the Amit Hub (the chat icon on the right edge, and the Communications page). Friends by link or code, group chats, photos, files and voice messages, read receipts, a live transcript, and a read-aloud player that follows the words. AMIT IS IN THE CHAT: press the Amit icon and he joins and listens; he stays quiet while people talk, comes in after a pause with a question or a thought, answers at once when his name is said, and turns himself off if nobody replies. If you are the only person there, everything you write is for him. The Ask Amit button at the top right opens your own private chat with Amit, who greets you and answers questions, including voice messages and anything he can look up on the web or in Amit’s own notes. The envelope button sends a private message to Amit’s team (it lands in the team inbox in the Hub, Amit confirms in the chat, tells you when it has been seen, and brings the reply back into the chat; reminders go out after 24 and 48 working hours, never on the Sabbath weekend). Built to keep young people safe: a birth date kept in About Me, and parents and guardians decide whether their child may chat and can read their child’s chats until they turn 18. WHISPER MODE lets you speak into any program on a Windows computer, not just the chat: a message box, a web address bar, a search box, your code editor. It comes with Amit Live, Amit's small helper. Hold the right mouse button where you want the words, wait until Amit's gold icon appears next to your pointer, speak, and let go. Your words show in a small box as you talk and are typed into the field as you speak; when a sentence ends, Amit tidies it with capitals and punctuation. Letting go can also press Enter to send what you said (a setting, off until you turn it on). A quick tap of the button is still a normal click. Amit can only type into a text box that has the focus, so click inside one first; if you are not in a text box, it tells you and types nothing and sends nothing, so your words are never lost silently in the wrong place. In the small Amit window you open from the taskbar you can change the button, how long you hold it, whether it presses Enter, whether it only types into a text box, and how long it stays ready (30 seconds, 5, 10 or 30 minutes, or all the time): keeping it ready uses about 400 MB of memory (up to half a gigabyte), so you can choose to have it start only when you press the button. That window also explains what it is and has a button that opens the Hub. It needs an internet connection and Microsoft Edge or Google Chrome. While you hold the button your voice goes to your browser's speech service; Amit does not record or keep it, and it uses none of your Claude account. First use: studying Scripture together. Its notes: AmitChat/CLAUDE.md and AmitChat/Sessions.md.
links: Open the Hub (chat icon on the right)

apps.name: The Council
apps.desc: A multi-AI brainstorming room. A question goes to several AI voices in rounds, each answer is recorded, and the room synthesizes them.

apps.name: Computer Health
apps.desc: A live health dashboard for a PC. A small local helper called Amit Live, installed once (it also carries Whisper mode, which lets you speak into any program), reads hardware, sensors and system resources, and the page shows readings, diagnostics and history. It is the free side of Computer Value, the product meant to fund the mission.

apps.name: Amit Live
apps.desc: Amit on the person's own computer, connected to all of Amit. The AURORA is the ring that opens when you hold the trigger mouse button (right by default) anywhere in Windows; its centre Amit icon is Ask Amit and opens the AMIT LIVE WINDOW, a small floating chat under the person's own sign-in. CONNECTED TO: the Hub (My Morning, Chats, About Me voice, Appearance theme), AmitChat (the chat itself, one chat per day), Computer Health (the local helper and the Computer Health tab), My Words (voice commands, shortcuts and fixes), Show Amit (screenshots; its Show Amit button sends a shot to Amit in today's chat and Amit reads it), Whisper (dictate into any program), and every application on this list, because the Amit that answers reads this list and each application's own notes. Tabs: Ask Amit, My Computer, My Words, Computer Health. The first open each day is the morning wake-up (greeting, the person's music, icons for weather, computer and the day's to-dos); later opens that day are a small chat. Needs the small local Amit helper (installed with Computer Health) and the internet; with no internet it says so plainly and offers Windows network settings. Questions go to the answering computer and the person's own Claude account.

apps.name: Show Amit
apps.desc: Show Amit is the screenshot tool of Amit Live (the Aurora ring: choose Show Amit, drag over any part of the screen). A shot opens in an editor where the person can zoom, write words, draw, add layers and save it to PicturesShow Amit. THE SHOW AMIT BUTTON in that editor sends the shot to Amit: it saves what is on screen (as Save View does, named after the title), the Amit Live window opens on the person's Ask Amit chat for today, posts the picture there under their own sign-in with the title and any words typed on it, and asks Amit to look. Amit reads the picture and answers in the chat. The picture is private to that chat; the link Amit uses is made by the person's own sign-in and works 10 minutes for that one file; the helper deletes its copy after answering. Needs the local Amit helper, the internet and the answering computer.

apps.desc: Bookkeeping built for small businesses. Includes the General Journal with drill-down and an audit trail, a monthly outstanding-balance tracker, and sensitive fields locked with a personal PIN.

apps.desc: The field-capture companion for AmitBooks. Photograph receipts and documents on a phone and send them in for processing.

apps.name: AmitCoder

apps.name: Medical Prep

apps.name: AmitRoll
apps.desc: A dice-and-number arithmetic game for kids and adults, rebuilt from "Ready, Set, Roll," a game Ryan made about fifteen years ago for his daughter. You roll dice and cover number cards by using the dice (adding first, then subtracting, multiplying and dividing as the levels rise), you decide when to bank your points or risk another roll, and the clock gets shorter as you improve. Beginners get help buttons where Amit shows a better play. Notes: AmitRoll/CLAUDE.md and AmitRoll/Sessions.md.

apps.name: AmitCapacity
apps.desc: Shows, with numbers measured on two days of real use, what a person gets for $30 a month: $20 to Claude for the AI on their own account and $10 to Amit for premium access to the whole Amit suite. For a normal question (about 20 words asked, about 150 words answered, about 12 seconds) that is about 125 questions in a 5-hour window, about 1,450 a week and about 6,200 a month on Claude Pro, with ordinary questions and deep research questions shown separately, and the same in hours of use. Tabs: The Story (the recorded conversation between the desktop Amit who builds and measures and the online Amit who answers in the Hub chat, with the screenshots, shown only to the owner), The Numbers, Receipts (each signed-in person's own answers as a share of a window and a week), and Ask Amit. Notes: AmitCapacity/CLAUDE.md and AmitCapacity/Sessions.md.

apps.name: AmitFix
apps.desc: THE ONE PLACE TO INSTALL, FIX, QUIET OR REMOVE ANYTHING AMIT PUTS ON A COMPUTER. If anyone asks how to install Amit's helper, how to fix it, how to turn voice typing off, or how to remove Amit, send them here: AmitFix (the Help button at the bottom of the Hub's right rail also opens it). Amit himself lives online and is never removed; what lives on a Windows computer is Amit's helper (the small program and watchers behind voice typing in any program and Computer Health). Pages: Director's Chair, Send It, Our Heart, What's On My Computer, Verify It and Check It. Tabs under the Director's Chair: Start here (tell it what is happening and it ticks the right fixes), Make it right (look first, restart, tidy up, reset voice typing, or a fresh start), Quiet on set (turn voice typing on or off, stop it starting with Windows, remove desktop shortcuts, forget what it kept), Browser & phone (sign out and clear what Amit saved in a browser, any device), Wrap (Remove Amit: closes the helper, turns off start-with-Windows, deletes its files, saved data and shortcuts, then checks and shows that it is really gone), and Install Amit (one button downloads the installer, with the steps in plain words). Removing and reinstalling is also how the helper is updated, with no manual steps. Choices go on a call sheet and download as one small file, or Remove-Amit.exe does the whole removal in one click. The page knows where you came from (the Hub, an email, a QR code, a phone) and opens straight to the right fix. It can be sent by link, email, text, share, QR code or a one-page PDF. It lists everything Amit puts on a computer in plain words (including Node.js and Claude Code, which the installer adds only if they are missing, for AmitBooks receipts, and which removal deliberately leaves in place), and the program is readable text before you run it. Windows will say 'unknown publisher' because there is no code-signing certificate yet. It also holds a welcome, a farewell and a come-back note from the people who made Amit. VERIFY IT: a page (and a plain-text file, AmitFix/Verify.txt) for anyone who worries Amit's helper might be malware. They copy one packet into any AI or a security forum and ask for a hostile review. The packet says what the programs are, names every behavior that looks suspicious and why it is there (a system-wide mouse hook for voice typing, typing into other programs, a localhost-only web server, hidden PowerShell, start-with-Windows, optional Node.js and Claude Code, no code-signing certificate yet, developer-only parts that are inert on ordinary computers), gives claims to try to disprove, the SHA-256 fingerprint of every file, the complete list of web addresses the code can reach, and how to test safely on a spare computer. Personal details are left out. Amit asks to be checked and would rather be corrected than trusted. CHECK IT: a read-only program (Amit_Check.cmd, from the Check It page) that compares every file Amit installed on a computer against the SHA-256 fingerprints Amit published, and also checks for extra files, the start-with-Windows entry, the two web-link handlers, desktop shortcuts, what the helper listens on, and whether the programs are signed. It fetches the fingerprint list a second time straight from GitHub so a tampered web page alone cannot fool it. The result is a plain report (user name and computer name masked), already copied to the clipboard, with a verdict: ALL MATCH, OLDER VERSION (update, then check again) or DIFFERENCES FOUND (remove, reinstall, re-check, and tell Amit's makers). It is for both worries: a person who fears malware on their computer, and the makers, who want to know if their own files were ever tampered with. The report is meant to be pasted into an independent AI together with the Verify packet. DIRECTION (Ryan, 2026-10-26, not built yet): anything new that needs a connection on someone's computer will get its own tab here, so this stays the single hub for installing, fixing and removing. Notes: AmitFix/CLAUDE.md and AmitFix/Sessions.md.

groups.title: Other applications we built (not part of Amit)

apps.name: Yamaha Recon Capture
apps.desc: A phone application for a dealership client's monthly bookkeeping reconciliation, and it works well. Photograph the three source documents (daily POS reports, the merchant-services statement and the bank statement), tag them by month, and they upload to a live viewer that can be reviewed from the phone or the desktop.

apps.name: AeyeQ — Dog Race Analyzer
apps.desc: A greyhound race analysis tool for Wheeling track programs. It scores each dog with a custom weighted rating (form, class move, post, speed and break), then tracks predicted results against actual ones so the weights can be tuned.

planned.name: Amit Assembly
planned.desc: Designed, not built. A construction estimating, change-order, bidding and vendor-pricing platform, rebuilt from a ten-year-old Access system. It will share client and vendor data with AmitBooks.

planned.name: Amit Companion
planned.desc: The discipleship companion: testimony tracking, daily encouragement, and a deeper walk over time. Planned; the Hub's daily features carry part of this for now.

planned.name: Amit Stewardship
planned.desc: Home, vehicle and equipment lifecycle tracking, built the way Computer Health is: catalog the asset, check its health, and turn maintenance into Pursuits. A future concept.

planned.name: God Talk — The Ten Commandments
planned.desc: One commandment studied per session, studied for its intent. The content exists as a written study; the interactive application has not been built.

planned.name: Computer Value
planned.desc: The paid diagnostic and certification report for custom PCs, the revenue engine meant to keep the rest of Amit free. Computer Health is its free side; the paid tier is not built.
